header: GOLD AND SILVER IN INDIA, from the page of the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). I use it because its rates are the ones the trade follows. The page carries today's rates in labelled cells (lblGold999_AM ...) and, for its own chart, the PM rate of every trading day for the last four months or so (hidden fields HdnGold and HdnSilver, as JSON). That is the "trend", and it is OFFICIAL data, not an estimate. Gold is per 10 grams, silver per kilogram, before GST and making charges. 24 carat = 999 purity, 22 carat = 916 purity. This file is pure: the page's text goes in, the numbers come out (tested on a saved copy of the page).

members.name: date
doc: YYYY-MM-DD

members.name: est
doc: I set this to true for a day worked out from the gold/silver ETF (before IBJA's own page begins), and never for an IBJA rate.

members.name: carried
doc: Set on the first point of the year when there is no rate for that exact day (a weekend or a holiday). It holds the day of the rate it really is (the last one before).

symbols.name: Estimate
doc: Records how the days before IBJA's page begins were worked out, and how close that method came on the days where both exist.

members.name: from
doc: The first and last estimated day, YYYY-MM-DD.

members.name: officialFrom
doc: The first day of IBJA's own record.

members.name: checkedDays
doc: How many days exist in both records, that is, the days I checked the method on.

members.name: gold
doc: Average and largest difference (percent) from IBJA's rate on those days.

members.name: savedThrough
doc: Set when the fund prices are the copy kept with the app because the live source did not answer: it is the last day that copy covers.

members.name: gold24Per10g
doc: Today's opening (AM) rates. I add PM when IBJA has published it.

members.name: session
doc: Which session these rates are from: "AM" or "PM".

members.name: asOf
doc: Set only when IBJA has no rates for today (Saturday, Sunday, a central government holiday, or a working day's morning before the first rate is up). It is the date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last day IBJA published, whose closing (PM) rates these are.

members.name: notPublished
doc: The page's own words when it has no rates for today ("Rates are not published on Central Govt. Holidays & SAT/SUN", or on a working day's morning "Rates will be uploaded soon").

members.name: change
members.type: { gold24: { abs: number; pct: number } | null; gold22: { abs: number; pct: number } | null; silver: { abs: number; pct: number } | null }
doc: The change against the last PM close in the history.

members.name: history
doc: The PM rate of each trading day, oldest first.

members.name: rangeText
doc: "13 Jul to 11 Nov 2026"

members.name: estimate
doc: Present when I added earlier days by estimate (they are marked est. in `history`).

members.name: estimateUnavailable
doc: Says why the earlier days could not be added this time; the chart then shows IBJA's own days only.

symbols.name: parseIbja
symbols.sig: export function parseIbja(html: string): MetalRates | null
doc: Returns the rates and the trend from the text of the IBJA page, or null when the page does not hold them (the page changed, or it is not the page).

members.name: dates
doc: Dates are YYYY-MM-DD (Indian date), oldest first.

symbols.name: parseEtfSeries
symbols.sig: export function parseEtfSeries(json: unknown): EtfSeries | null
doc: Returns the daily closes from a Yahoo chart answer (range 1y, interval 1d), or null when it does not hold a usable record.

symbols.name: fit
symbols.sig: function fit(history: MetalPoint[], pick: (p: MetalPoint) => number, etf: EtfSeries): { scale: number; avgPct: number; maxPct: number; days: number } | null
symbols.returns: { scale: number; avgPct: number; maxPct: number; days: number } | null
doc: This gives the scale from the ETF to IBJA, worked out from the days both exist. It is null when the two do not follow each other closely, and then I make no estimate.

symbols.name: extendHistory
symbols.sig: export function extendHistory(rates: MetalRates, gold: EtfSeries | null, silver: EtfSeries | null, savedThrough?: string, now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): MetalRates
doc: Returns IBJA's rates with the earlier days added by estimate (see above). When no honest estimate can be made, I return the rates themselves unchanged.

symbols.name: looksLikeGoldAnswer
symbols.sig: export function looksLikeGoldAnswer(x: unknown): x is MetalRates
doc: Tells whether a saved answer of the gold route is the shape the card draws (the rates and a record of days). I never show a saved copy that is not.

behaviours: the page is read
24 carat is 999 purity and 22 carat is 916: today's opening rates per 10 g
silver per kg and per gram
the trend is IBJA's own PM rates of every trading day, oldest first, four months or so
every point has a gold 24, a gold 22 and a silver rate, the 22 carat below the 24
the change is against the last PM close: gold 24 down about 1.6 percent
a page without the rates (it changed, or it is another page) gives nothing, not wrong numbers
a PM rate, when published, replaces the AM one
a point missing from the silver chart is left out, never invented
the ETF record is read: about a year of daily closes, oldest first, Indian dates
a record that is not an ETF chart (or too short) is refused
earlier days are added before IBJA's first day, all marked as estimates, and IBJA's own days are untouched and not marked
the chart BEGINS ON THE SAME DATE A YEAR BACK (13 Nov 2025 when today is 13 Nov 2026), that day's own estimate, not marked as carried
when the date a year back is a Saturday (15 Nov 2025) the chart still begins on it, holding the figure of Friday 14 Nov, marked as carried; no point is dated before it
the range text begins on that date too
the estimate says how close it was on the days where both records exist: well under one percent on average
the 22 carat estimate keeps IBJA's 916/999 relation and every estimated point is complete
the range text names the year of both ends
today's rates and the change are those of IBJA, not of the estimate
without both ETF records nothing is added (the rates come back unchanged)
an ETF record that does not follow IBJA closely enough is not used
a record that stops well before IBJA's first day (a hole would be left) is not used
when the saved copy is used the estimate says so
the copy kept with the app is a readable year of both records, as recent as its date says, and gives an estimate
a record with no earlier days adds nothing
on a day with no rates the last published day's closing (PM) rates are given, dated, with the page's own words
their change is against the closing rate of the day before (12 Nov: 137692), and the chart still ends on that last published day
an ordinary day carries no date or note
on a working day's morning, before the first rate is up, the last published day's closing (PM) rates are shown, dated, with the page's own words
the morning page has the message and no rate cell, so before this it was an error (the 503 the card showed)
a page that has no rates and says something else is still an error, never a guess
a page with no rates and no such message is still an error, and so is a message with no days before it
